rolls.D20 Test: The collective term for the three kinds of d20 roll: ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws. Effects that modify 'D20 Tests' modify all three.
rolls.Ability Check: A D20 Test to overcome a challenge, using one of the six abilities and possibly a skill or tool proficiency.
rolls.Saving Throw: A D20 Test to resist or avoid a threat.
rolls.Attack Roll: A D20 Test made to hit with a weapon, an Unarmed Strike, or an attack-roll spell.
rolls.Advantage: Roll two d20s and use the higher. Multiple sources never stack.
rolls.Disadvantage: Roll two d20s and use the lower. Multiple sources never stack. One Advantage and one Disadvantage cancel to a single flat d20 regardless of how many of each you have.
rolls.Proficiency Bonus: A level-based bonus added to D20 Tests you are proficient in. +2 at levels 1-4, +3 at 5-8, +4 at 9-12, +5 at 13-16, +6 at 17-20.
rolls.Expertise: Your Proficiency Bonus is doubled for a specific skill or tool.
rolls.Heroic Inspiration: A resource you can expend to reroll any one die immediately after rolling it. You must use the new result. You can hold only one at a time.
rolls.Difficulty Class (DC): The number an ability check or saving throw must meet or beat.
rolls.Passive Perception: 10 + your Wisdom (Perception) check bonus. Used when the DM does not want to call for a roll.
rolls.Round Down: Whenever you divide and get a fraction, round down unless a rule says otherwise.

timeAndAction.Round: One full cycle through the initiative order, representing about 6 seconds.
timeAndAction.Turn: One participant's portion of a round.
timeAndAction.Action: The single main thing you do on your turn.
timeAndAction.Bonus Action: A second, smaller action available only when a feature, spell, or effect grants one, and only on a turn where you also take an action. One per turn maximum.
timeAndAction.Reaction: An action taken outside your turn in response to a defined trigger. One per round; you regain it at the start of your next turn.
timeAndAction.Initiative: 1d20 + Dexterity modifier, rolled once at the start of combat to set turn order.
timeAndAction.Surprise: A creature caught unawares at the start of combat has Disadvantage on its Initiative roll. In 2014 it lost its whole first turn instead.

space.Speed: How many feet you can move on your turn.
space.Difficult Terrain: Each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot. Multiple sources in one space do not stack.
space.Half Cover: +2 to AC and Dexterity saving throws.
space.Three-Quarters Cover: +5 to AC and Dexterity saving throws.
space.Total Cover: Cannot be targeted directly by an attack or a spell. Only the single highest degree of cover applies.
space.Size Categories: Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, Gargantuan.
space.Carrying Capacity: Strength score x 15 pounds. Push, drag, or lift up to Strength score x 30 pounds.

areasOfEffect.Emanation: An area of effect that extends in straight lines from a CREATURE OR OBJECT in all directions, out to a distance the effect specifies. It moves with the creature or object that is its origin, unless the effect is instantaneous or stationary - no action is needed to reposition it. IMPORTANT DEFAULT MOST TOOLS GET WRONG: an Emanation's origin (the creature or object it comes from) is NOT included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise. Individual features often override this - the Paladin's Aura of Protection says 'You and your allies in the aura', which explicitly opts the Paladin in - but the general default is exclusion. Never assume the origin creature is affected by its own Emanation unless the feature says so.
areasOfEffect.Sphere: An area extending in straight lines from a POINT of origin in all directions. Unlike an Emanation it is anchored to a location, not a creature, so it does not move.
areasOfEffect.Cone: An area extending in straight lines from a point of origin in a chosen direction. Its width at any point equals its distance from the origin.
areasOfEffect.Cube: An area extending in straight lines from a point of origin on one face of the cube.
areasOfEffect.Cylinder: An area extending in straight lines from a point of origin at the centre of the circular top or bottom face.
areasOfEffect.Line: An area extending in a straight path from its origin, with a stated width.
areasOfEffect.Targeting rule: To determine whether a space is in an area of effect, trace a line from the point of origin. If an obstruction provides Total Cover along that line, the space is excluded. Nothing less than Total Cover blocks an area of effect.
areasOfEffect.Emanation vs 2014 aura: 2014 wrote auras as 'friendly creatures within 10 feet of you' with no formal keyword, leaving wall and cover interactions ambiguous. 2024 defines Emanation explicitly, which resolves those questions.
areasOfEffect.Blocking rule: General Area of Effect rule, which applies to Emanations too: 'If all straight lines extending from the point of origin to a location in the area of effect are blocked, that location isn't included in the area of effect. To block a line, an obstruction must provide Total Cover.' So nothing less than Total Cover excludes a space.

damageAndHealing.Commonly resisted: Fire and Poison are the two most widely resisted or immune types across the monster manual, followed by nonmagical Bludgeoning/Piercing/Slashing, Necrotic (undead), and Cold. Force and Psychic are resisted by almost nothing, which makes them the most reliable damage types in the game.
damageAndHealing.Resistance: Damage of that type is halved. Resistance is applied after all other modifiers and never stacks with itself.
damageAndHealing.Vulnerability: Damage of that type is doubled.
damageAndHealing.Immunity: Damage of that type has no effect, or a condition cannot affect you.
damageAndHealing.Hit Points: A measure of durability. At 0 HP a player character falls Unconscious and begins making Death Saving Throws.
damageAndHealing.Hit Point Dice: Class-based dice (d10 for a Paladin) spent on a Short Rest to heal. In 2024 you regain ALL of them on a Long Rest.
damageAndHealing.Temporary Hit Points: A buffer lost before real Hit Points. They never stack - gaining new ones means choosing to keep the old pool or take the new one. They are not healing and cannot revive an unconscious creature. Lost at the end of a Long Rest.
damageAndHealing.Critical Hit: A natural 20 on an attack roll. Roll all of the attack's damage dice twice and add them together. Flat modifiers are not doubled.
damageAndHealing.Death Saving Throw: A plain 1d20 at the start of each of your turns at 0 HP. 10 or higher succeeds. Three successes make you Stable; three failures kill you. A natural 20 restores 1 HP; a natural 1 counts as two failures.
damageAndHealing.Stable: At 0 HP but no longer rolling death saves. Still Unconscious. Regains 1 HP after 1d4 hours if nothing else happens.
damageAndHealing.Instant Death: If leftover damage after dropping to 0 HP equals or exceeds your Hit Point maximum, you die outright.
damageAndHealing.Falling: 1d6 Bludgeoning damage per 10 feet fallen, to a maximum of 20d6, plus you land Prone.
damageAndHealing.Suffocation: You can hold your breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 + your Constitution modifier, minimum 30 seconds. After that you survive a number of rounds equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1) and then drop to 0 HP.
damageAndHealing.Bloodied: A creature at half its Hit Point maximum or fewer. New formal term in 2024, referenced by some features.

magic.Spell Slot: The resource expended to cast a leveled spell. You can expend only ONE per turn.
magic.Spell Level: A spell's tier, 1 through 9. A cantrip is level 0.
magic.Cantrip: A level 0 spell cast without expending a spell slot, at will.
magic.Ritual: A spell with the Ritual tag can be cast taking 10 minutes longer and expending no spell slot. You must have it prepared. In 2024 any class can do this.
magic.Concentration: Some spells require it. You can hold only one at a time. It ends if you cast another Concentration spell, fail a Constitution save after taking damage (DC 10 or half the damage, whichever is higher), become Incapacitated, or die.
magic.Spellcasting Focus: An item that replaces material components - a Holy Symbol for a Paladin. It cannot replace a component that has a listed gold-piece cost or that the spell consumes.
magic.Verbal (V): You must speak. Blocked while unable to speak, including while Incapacitated.
magic.Somatic (S): You need one free hand. A hand holding your Spellcasting Focus counts.
magic.Material (M): You need a free hand to access the components. Not consumed unless stated.
magic.Attunement: A bond required by some magic items, formed over a Short Rest. You can be attuned to at most 3 items at once.

senses.Blindsight: You can see within a stated range without relying on physical sight, including in Darkness and while Blinded.
senses.Darkvision: Within the stated range you treat Dim Light as Bright Light and Darkness as Dim Light. You discern colour in Darkness only as shades of grey.
senses.Tremorsense: You can pinpoint the location of creatures and moving objects in contact with the same surface, within range, without seeing them.
senses.Truesight: Within range you see in normal and magical Darkness, see Invisible creatures and objects, automatically detect illusions and succeed on saves against them, and perceive the true form of shapechanged or transformed creatures.
senses.Telepathy: You can speak mentally to a creature within range that knows at least one language. It cannot reply unless it also has telepathy.
senses.Bright Light / Dim Light / Darkness: Dim Light creates a Lightly Obscured area (Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight). Darkness creates a Heavily Obscured area, which effectively imposes the Blinded condition on anyone trying to see into it.

attitudes.Ally: A creature friendly to you or fighting on your side. This now has a hard rules meaning, which matters for auras and 'you and your allies' effects.

weaponProperties.Ammunition: You can make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire.
weaponProperties.Finesse: Use Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls, your choice.
weaponProperties.Heavy: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with it if your Strength (for a Melee weapon) or Dexterity (for a Ranged weapon) is below 13.
weaponProperties.Light: When you attack with it using the Attack action, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later that turn with a different Light weapon you are holding. You do not add your ability modifier to that extra attack's damage unless the modifier is negative.
weaponProperties.Loading: You can fire only one piece of ammunition per action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, regardless of how many attacks you could otherwise make.
weaponProperties.Reach: Adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, including for Opportunity Attacks.
weaponProperties.Thrown: You can throw it to make a ranged attack, drawing it as part of the attack.
weaponProperties.Two-Handed: Requires both hands when you attack with it.
weaponProperties.Versatile: Can be used one- or two-handed. The larger damage die in parentheses applies when used two-handed.
weaponProperties.Special: The weapon has a unique rule stated in its own entry.

note: Weapon properties are printed in the Equipment chapter rather than the Rules Glossary, but they are rules canon and belong in a study mode.
